text:
Maya: Heads up — inference pods are seeing intermittent 502/504s when calling model-registry in eu-west-3, looks constrained to AZ c
Maya: deploy-bot canary fired for model-registry-canary: 502 via private endpoint :grimacing:
deploy-bot: [ALERT] canary
  name: model-registry-canary
  result: 502
  target: vpce-0a1b2c3d
Liam: is that the interface endpoint (vpce) or a gateway?
Maya: iface endpoint (com.redwood.internal.model-registry) vpce-0a1b2c3d
Maya: quick test from bastion in azc: curl to vpce DNS succeeds
Maya: from a failing pod in autoscaling-group-asg-a (subnet-azc) we get timeout
Jules: could be route table differences or SG, posting checks
NetEng: can you paste the describe-vpc-endpoints output and subnet/eni list?
Maya: here — the vpce shows network interfaces in subnets az-a and az-b but NOT az-c

```
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d --region eu-west-3
{
  "VpcEndpoints": [
    {
      "VpcEndpointId": "vpce-0a1b2c3d",
      "VpcId": "vpc-0f1e2d3c",
      "ServiceName": "com.redwood.internal.model-registry",
      "VpcEndpointType": "Interface",
      "SubnetIds": ["subnet-az-a", "subnet-az-b"],
      "NetworkInterfaceIds": ["eni-aaa111", "eni-bbb222"],
      "PrivateDnsEnabled": true
    }
  ]
}
```

Liam: interesting — interface endpoints should have ENIs in all subnets you specified. If az-c subnet is missing, that explains pods hitting other egress paths
NetEng: I ran `describe-network-interfaces` filtered by vpce owner, looks like eni creation failed for az-c due to no available IPs in that subnet

```
aws ec2 describe-subnets --subnet-ids subnet-az-c --query 'Subnets[0].AvailableIpAddressCount' --output text
0
```

NetEng: az-c had AvailableIpAddressCount=0, so VPC endpoint couldn't allocate an ENI there
Maya: ohhh — so pods in az-c resolve to model-registry DNS but traffic goes out via NAT (since no ENI) and hits public endpoint, causing SNI mismatch and 502s
Jules: or if private hosted zone exists and points to a public A record, that could also route wrong — do we have any hosted zone overlapping?
Maya: checking Route53 private zones...
NetEng: we do have a private hosted zone model-registry.internal that was created years ago for another account, but it has A records that point to an ALB in the consumer VPC, not the vpce aliases
Maya: so two problems: endpoint ENI missing in az-c due to IP exhaustion, and a conflicting private hosted zone that resolves to non-vpce addresses for some pods
Liam: that explains why bastion (using system DNS) worked but pods didn't — pod DNS could be using kube-dns view that picks up the private hosted zone record
sre-oncall: quick mitigation options?
NetEng: immediate: (1) create a small Route53 private hosted zone override in this VPC that aliases model-registry.internal -> vpce-0a1b2c3d (if PrivateDnsEnabled is on, it should have created an alias but conflict prevents it) (2) free up IPs in subnet-az-c by moving some non-critical ENIs or expanding subnet CIDR (3) re-create endpoint after freeing IPs so it attaches ENI to az-c
Jules: steps I'd run now:

```
# check for conflicting hosted zones
aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-name --dns-name "model-registry.internal" --query 'HostedZones' --region eu-west-3

# show endpoint DNS names
aws ec2 describe-vpc-endpoints --vpc-endpoint-ids vpce-0a1b2c3d --query 'VpcEndpoints[0].DnsEntries' --output json
```

Maya: I can repro the DNS mismatch locally in a failing pod: dig @10.0.0.2 model-registry.internal +short -> 3.80.20.11 (public ALB IP)
Maya: digging vpce DNS from bastion returns vpce-abcdef.vpce-svc.amazonaws.com alias which is correct
NetEng: while we fix infra, we can add a pod mutating config to force node-local dns or set up stub domain to point model-registry.internal to the vpce private IP — short-term hack
Liam: note: because traffic goes via NAT when ENI is missing, we saw unexpected egress to public and some failed TLS handshakes because client certificate validation expects the internal SAN — that'll be noisy and costy
Maya: what's the plan for permanent fix?
NetEng: schedule window to (A) allocate /28 to remedy available IPs in subnet-az-c and attach additional ENIs so endpoint can create its interface there; (B) remove the conflicting private hosted zone or migrate its records to use alias to the vpce; (C) re-create endpoint with PrivateDnsEnabled=true to ensure Route53 alias targets are set by AWS; (D) add monitoring alert for AvailableIpAddressCount < 10 for critical subnets
sre-oncall: created incident: INC-2026-042, tagging owners and setting priority P2
Maya: will implement the temporary stub-domain override to stop canaries from failing in the mean time
Jules: leaving notes in runbook: "interface endpoint ENI failures can be caused by subnet IP exhaustion or private hosted zone conflicts — check both"
NetEng: also recommend using endpoint subnet selection with subnets that have headroom or use /27 for worker subnets in future
Maya: thanks everyone — will follow up with a short postmortem once fixed :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: [INFO] canary paused until DNS override applied
